 Learn more Coherent's modeled fair value has shifted from about US$405.22 to about US$387.80, giving investors a fresh reference point for how the market's price targets are evolving. Recent analyst research links these changes to a balance of enthusiasm for AI driven optics and data center demand, along with a more cautious view on valuation, execution risk, and competition. As you read on, you will see how to interpret these moving targets and track the narrative around Coherent as new data comes through. 
 Stay updated as the Fair Value for Coherent shifts by adding it to your watchlist or portfolio . Alternatively, explore our Community to discover new perspectives on Coherent. 
 What Wall Street Has Been Saying 
 🐂 Bullish Takeaways 
 Several firms, including Deutsche Bank, Jefferies, Needham, Rosenblatt and StoneX, have initiated or reiterated positive views on Coherent that focus on AI driven data center demand, longer order visibility and capacity expansion in areas such as the 6 inch InP fab. 
 Jefferies, Raymond James and B. Riley highlight prior quarters where Coherent issued guidance that they describe as supportive of higher long term revenue potential, with some commentary pointing to order books that extend into 2028. 
 Bernstein and Deutsche Bank frame Coherent as closely tied to AI networking and high speed transceivers, with Bernstein describing networking and optical companies as potential structural beneficiaries of AI infrastructure spending. 
 Northland's upgrade of Coherent to Outperform in November 2026 follows what it describes as steep share pullbacks and growing recognition of the value of scarce photonic device capability for large AI chip suppliers. 
 🐻 Bearish Takeaways 
 Multiple firms have adjusted price targets lower over recent months, including JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, Susquehanna and B. Riley, which ties part of its reduction to multiple compression across AI focused optical stocks. 
 Northland and Morgan Stanley flag execution and competitive risks, particularly around pluggable transceivers and qualification of high powered lasers for CPO implementations, which they suggest can limit earnings leverage and valuation.

 How This Changes the Fair Value For Coherent 
 Fair value in the model has shifted from about US$405.22 to about US$387.80. 
 Revenue growth has been adjusted from about 39.40% to about 39.38%. 
 Net profit margin has been updated from about 18.39% to about 18.48%. 
 Future P/E has moved from about 35.41x to about 33.73x. 
 The discount rate has changed slightly from 8.91% to 8.90%.

 Key threats that could disrupt this path, including low cost competition in optical transceivers, heavy capital investment needs, cyclical end markets, and reliance on a small group of major customers.
